conviction_note: The findings point both ways. Q3 RevPAR will almost certainly clear Marriott's 3.5-4% guide on the evidence of three peers that reported after Marriott last spoke (Hilton +5.8%, Hyatt +7.2%, IHG +5.3%, all with the US at +7-8%). Against that, the reaction turns on the Q4/FY guide, where Marriott carries the biggest Middle East book of the US majors in that region's peak quarter, and Hilton was sold 2.1% for exactly that line. The stock is also 0.7% off its 52-week high after +11.8% in 20 days, and this name sold a raised guide for -7% in August. impact_sum -0.4 and the scaled -0.09 (p_up 49 on a 4.5% abs move) agree in sign and size: a near-zero lean with a large two-sided move.
bar: Company guide (2026-08-03 Q2 release): Q3 global RevPAR +3.5% to +4.0%, Q3 adj. EPS $2.74-2.82, FY RevPAR +3.0-3.5%, FY adj. EPS $11.64-11.81, NUG toward low end of 4.5-5% (https://www.franchising.com/news/20260803_marriott_international_reports_second_quarter_2026_results.html ; https://finviz.com/news/375971/marriott-shares-slip-despite-earnings-beat-as-revenue-falls-short-of-expectations). Street EPS is disputed: $2.86 with a $2.92 whisper and ~$7.04bn revenue (Earnings Whispers preview 2026-10-26, https://finviz.com/news/407878/marriotts-q3-test-can-us-momentum-and-new-card-deals-clear-a-bar-above-guidance), ~$2.83 (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/MAR/earnings-forecasts), ~$2.88 (MarketBeat), $2.93 (undated, https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/MAR). There is no published Q3 RevPAR consensus. print_vs_bar_pct is my expected EPS of ~$2.93 against $2.86, on a ~1.25pt RevPAR beat. The EPS bar is disputed, so the reported-quarter size is kept modest. The RevPAR bar is the company's own guide.
positioning_check: Short interest: 6.73M shares as of the 2026-09-30 settlement, 4.2-4.3 days to cover (https://shortsqueeze.com/?symbol=MAR, page dated 2026-10-22; https://massive.com/quote/mar). That is about 2.5% of float and not a crowded short, so there is no squeeze mechanism against a negative. Baseline: 25d skew +2.54 vol points (downside mildly paid), put/call OI 0.65, event-implied move 3.97% (straddle 4.61%), 20d run-up +11.76%, 5d +2.68%, -0.7% from the 52-week high. Price into the print (Yahoo daily): 390.23 on Oct 27 (-1.1% on Hilton's print day), 399.65 on Oct 29 (+1.3% on Hyatt's), 401.91 on Oct 30. So about 2.3% of peer read-through has already been taken in the last three sessions.

findings.finding: Three peers that reported after Marriott's last update (2026-08-03) printed Q3 RevPAR far above Marriott's own Q3 global guide of +3.5% to +4.0%. Hilton system +5.8% with US +7.0%, Europe +6.5% and MEA -5.6% (8-K, 2026-10-27). Hyatt comparable system +7.2% with US +8.2%, luxury leading, and the FY RevPAR guide raised to +5.0-5.5% (8-K, 2026-10-29). IHG global +5.3% with Americas +6.8% (2026-10-22). Marriott's US & Canada is about two-thirds of its system and luxury/upper-upscale heavy, and CoStar put luxury/upper-upscale RevPAR at about +10.2% from Memorial Day to Labor Day. That implies Marriott Q3 global RevPAR of roughly +5%, about 1.25pt above the top of its guide, and a mechanical FY RevPAR raise from 3.0-3.5% to about 3.75-4.25%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-08-03 Marriott beat EPS ($3.19 vs ~$3.05) and raised FY RevPAR, and the stock fell -6.97% on a revenue miss. On 2026-02-10 the stock rose +8.5% and on 2025-11-04 +3.16% (baseline). Peers this week: Hilton beat RevPAR, raised FY RevPAR and fell -2.1% on Oct 27. Hyatt beat by more, raised FY RevPAR by about a point and rose +6.3% on Oct 29 (Yahoo daily closes).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. MAR rose about 2.3% from Oct 27 to Oct 30 and is 0.7% off its high. But the published Street EPS ($2.83-2.88 on most sources) sits barely above the top of the company's $2.74-2.82 guide, which is what a model with Q3 RevPAR near 4% gives. If the Street had moved to +5% RevPAR, consensus would read about $2.92-2.97 rather than $2.86. Only the whisper ($2.92) gets there.
findings.independence: Three separate primary documents point the same way: Hilton 8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001585689/000158568926000049/q32026earningsrelease.htm , IHG Q3 trading update https://www.ihgplc.com/en/news-and-media/news-releases/2026/third-quarter-trading-update-to-30-september-2026 , and CoStar's segment commentary via https://capitalanalyticsassociates.com/luxury-hotels-emerge-as-bright-spots-in-uneven-us-market/ . All are proxies for Marriott, not Marriott's own number.

findings.finding: The Q4/FY guide is exposed to the Middle East in its peak quarter and to the midterms. Marriott said on its Q2 call that Q4 is normally about 35% of its Middle East full-year revenue, that Q4 2025 had big ADR-lifting events, and that Q4 RevPAR would be 'a bit lower than Q3'. Hilton (2026-10-27) guided Q4 RevPAR to only +3.0-3.5%, flagged an 'increased impact from the Middle East' and cut its FY EBITDA expectation for the Middle East and timeshare fees despite raising RevPAR, and its stock fell 2.1% that day. Accor said UAE RevPAR was still about -20% year on year in Q3 (2026-10-22). Marriott has the largest Gulf footprint of the US majors, so a Q4 fee/EBITDA guide below the Street and an FY EBITDA raise smaller than the RevPAR beat implies is a real risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-08-03 a raised FY RevPAR guide, with NUG at the low end on Middle East construction delays and investment spending raised, was sold -6.97% (baseline; https://finviz.com/news/375971/marriott-shares-slip-despite-earnings-beat-as-revenue-falls-short-of-expectations). Peer on the same line this week: Hilton -2.1% on a Q4 guide dragged by the Middle East.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock is at its high with +11.8% in 20 days and only mild put skew (+2.54). That is not the shape of a market braced for a Q4 guide trimmed on the Middle East. If it were priced, the skew and the run-up would look like Hilton's after its print, not a stock 0.7% from its high.
findings.independence: Marriott's own Q2 call (https://transcripts.platformaeronaut.com/transcripts/MAR-2Q26-transcript) on Q4 seasonality. Accor Q3 on UAE -20% (https://www.businesstravelnewseurope.com/Accommodation/Accor-Q3-RevPAR-rises-as-Middle-East-impact-eases). Hilton commentary (https://hospitality-on.com/en/hospitality/europe-carries-hilton-third-quarter-while-middle-east-holds-back-outlook). This shares the Hilton 8-K with finding 1 but rests on a different line of it.

findings.finding: US demand stayed strong into Q4, which supports the US half of the guide. US hotel RevPAR was +5.5% in the week of 11-17 October 2026 (occupancy +3.1%, ADR +2.3%; CoStar via Hospitality Net, published 2026-10-23), after +14.2% in the week of 20-26 September on the Rosh Hashanah shift. Hyatt cited 'momentum after Labor Day' in raising its FY guide. This sits against Hilton's Q4 system guide of +3.0-3.5% and gives Marriott room for a firmer US Q4 comment than Hilton gave.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not separately observable for Marriott. Hyatt's post-Labor Day momentum comment came with a raise and +6.3% on Oct 29.
findings.why_not_priced: These are weekly industry series that most of the Street reads, so they are largely priced. The fact is filed small because it bears directly on how Marriott frames Q4 US against Hilton's cautious +3-3.5%.
findings.independence: Hyatt 8-K, post-Labor Day momentum (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001468174/000146817426000029/q32026earningsrelease.htm); CoStar week of 20-26 September (https://www.hospitalitynet.org/news/4134703/us-hotel-results-for-week-ending-26-september). Industry proxy, not company-confirmed.

findings.finding: Setup into the print: MAR is up 11.76% in 20 days and 8.7% since the Q2 report (vs S&P +1.4%), sits 0.7% off its 52-week high, and Street EPS ($2.86) already sits above the top of the company's Q3 guide ($2.74-2.82), with a $2.92 whisper. The last time it entered a print after a run, with a guide raise in hand (2026-08-03), it fell 6.97%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline reactions: -6.97, +1.28, +8.5, +3.16, +0.23, +1.9, -5.4. Five of seven up, median |move| 3.16%; both negative reactions were 5-7% drops.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-up is itself the price. The finding is that the bar for a positive reaction has risen above the guide-top consensus, and the whisper shows it. Short interest is about 2.5% of float, so there is no short base to squeeze on a beat.
findings.independence: Baseline tape (run_up_20d 11.76%, pct_from_52w_high -0.7) and Yahoo daily closes. Not independent of the reaction-history argument in finding 1, which is why each is sized small.

findings.finding: New Chase and American Express US co-brand card deals were expected to add about $30M of fees in H2 2026, with global card fees up in the high-30% range for 2026. This is already in the FY guide (Q2 call), and Japan yen weakness partly offsets it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The co-brand deal announcement drove a re-rating earlier in 2026 (https://rallies.ai/news/marriott-rallies-as-analysts-re-rate-stock-on-richer-credit-card-royalties-and-2026-outlook). Not visible as a print line since.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: it sits inside guidance. It is filed near zero for completeness, because an upside on card fees would show up in the Q3 fee line.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview repeats the $30M (https://finviz.com/news/407878/marriotts-q3-test-can-us-momentum-and-new-card-deals-clear-a-bar-above-guidance). Same original source.

findings.finding: The owner dispute over Bonvoy economics is unresolved. 51 owners representing nearly 1,000 hotels wrote to leadership (reported by the WSJ 2026-06-16) asking for a share of card fees. On the Q2 call management cut charge-out rates about 5%, raised award-night reimbursement and added an incentive of up to 50bp of room revenue, but declined to respond formally. Further concessions or cost (the incentive sits in owned/leased and other) could show up in Q3 margins or Q4 commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on this line. Owned/leased guidance has been cut twice (Earnings Whispers preview).
findings.why_not_priced: It is known but not quantified. A number on the call for the reimbursement or incentive cost would be new. If it were priced, the Street would carry an explicit owned/leased haircut beyond the guided $175-185M.
findings.independence: Q2 call transcript on the concessions (https://transcripts.platformaeronaut.com/transcripts/MAR-2Q26-transcript).

findings.finding: China and APAC look soft against Marriott's FY Greater China guide of +2-3%. In Q3, IHG Greater China RevPAR was -3.3% (weather, holiday timing), Hilton Asia Pacific -0.5%, and Accor said China declined, while Hyatt Greater China was +2.1%. Marriott's Greater China is a meaningful share of international rooms, so a Q3 China print near zero and a trimmed China guide are plausible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not observed as a driver of Marriott's last reactions, which turned on the US and the Middle East.
findings.why_not_priced: Small next to the US line. If it were priced, the China guide cut would already appear in the Street's international RevPAR assumptions, which no source shows.
findings.independence: Hilton 8-K, APAC -0.5% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001585689/000158568926000049/q32026earningsrelease.htm); Accor Q3 (https://www.businesstravelnewseurope.com/Accommodation/Accor-Q3-RevPAR-rises-as-Middle-East-impact-eases). Mixed: Hyatt +2.1%.

findings.finding: Net rooms growth was guided to the low end of 4.5-5% because of Middle East construction delays, against Hilton's 6-7% (reiterated at the midpoint 2026-10-27), and 2026 investment spending was raised to $1.25-1.35B on key money. A further NUG trim would extend the unit-growth gap to Hilton.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The NUG trim in August came with a -6.97% day, though the release-day coverage pinned that day on the revenue miss.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it is inside what the company already guided. It is filed small because the update lands on the print.

baseline_tension: The modest negative lean agrees with the mild put skew (+2.54) and leans against the +11.8% run-up continuing. The strongest single fact, a peer-implied Q3 RevPAR beat of about 1.25pt above guide, cuts the other way, so the net is near zero and p_up sits at 49 rather than lower.
lessons_applied: 'What has worked' (a peer's print landing after the company last spoke, leaving consensus stale): the peer RevPAR read-through went from +1.0 to +1.2. Lesson 1 (this name sold its August beat for -7%) is already in that size, so it is not cut twice.
Lesson 1 / core table (apply each lesson once): the positioning/run-up finding went from -0.8 to -0.6, because the beat-selling reaction function was already applied to the reported-quarter finding.

Asking 'what did the market miss' generates pessimism: draft sum -0.8 checked against the evidence. The US data is strongly positive, so p_up moved from 48 to 49 and the scaled number from -0.18 to -0.09.

Lesson 6 (verify the bar): the EPS consensus is disputed ($2.83/$2.86/$2.88/$2.93), but the company guide is sourced, so findings are sized against the RevPAR and EPS guide and the reported-quarter size stays modest.
Lesson 7: short interest was checked (about 2.5% of float, 4.2 days to cover, not crowded), and the negative sign agrees with the mild skew, so no shrink for a squeeze.
Left standing: the Middle East/Q4 guidance finding at -1.0, card fees, the owner dispute, China and NUG sizes.
